HDXBoxeR — bug worklist (branch correlation_V2)

Source: BUGS.md

Scratch review notes. Not a git-tracked deliverable. No R files were modified.

All findings below were verified by reading the code and, where marked [reproduced], by actually running the code against inst/extdata/All_results_table.csv with R 4.2.1.

Severity 1 — crashes / silently wrong results

[R/boxer_input_to_long.R:41] all_data_long_input() reads an undefined object path

Bug: the function argument is filepath, but the body reads path. There is no path object anywhere in the package, so the function throws on every call. Evidence:

all_data_long_input<-function(filepath){
  b1<-read.csv(path)                 # <- line 41: `path` is undefined

[reproduced] Error in read.table(file = file, ...) : object 'path' not found Impact: the function is 100% non-functional. Every call errors. Suggested fix: b1 <- read.csv(filepath).

[R/boxer_input_to_long.R:22-24] percent = TRUE mangles Protein.State and Experiment

Bug: the state/replicate split is done by splitting the column name on the literal letter "X". That only works for uptake columns (Unbound_X..Deut_1). With percent = TRUE output_tp() produces Unbound_Deut.._1, which contains no "X", so str_split_fixed(..., 'X', 2) returns the whole string in column 1 and "" in column 2. Evidence:

nms<-data.frame(str_split_fixed(v5$Experiment, 'X', 2))
v5$Protein.State <- str_sub(nms[,1], end = -2)      # line 23
v5$Experiment<-paste("X", nms[,2], sep="")          # line 24

[reproduced] boxer_input_to_long(file_nm, percent = TRUE) gives Protein.State = "Unbound_Deut.._" / "bound_Deut.._" and Experiment = "X" for all 768 rows (replicate identity completely lost). Correct output (percent = FALSE) is Protein.State = "Unbound"/"bound", Experiment = "X..Deut_1..3". Impact: percent = TRUE is a documented argument and silently produces a long-format table with unusable state labels and no replicate distinction. Any downstream group-by on Protein.State/Experiment is wrong, no error raised. Suggested fix: don’t parse on "X". Split on the known suffix instead, e.g. sub("_(X\\.\\.Deut|Deut\\.\\.)_[0-9]+$", "", nm) for the state and regmatches()/sub() for the replicate number, or better, carry the state/replicate mapping out of output_tp() directly.

[R/boxer_input_to_long.R:27 and :44] frac_deut is nonsense when percent = TRUE

Bug: frac_deut divides the value column by the number of exchangeable protons. That is only meaningful for uptake in Daltons. With percent = TRUE the column holds percent deuteration, so the result is “percent per residue”. Evidence:

v5$nb_prot<-nb_exch_deut(v5)
v5$frac_deut<-as.numeric(v5$X..Deut)/v5$nb_prot   # line 27

[reproduced] percent = TRUE gives frac_deut = 6.42, 5.91, 3.77, ... (should be 0–1). percent = FALSE correctly gives 0.63, 0.61, 0.32. Impact: silently wrong numbers in a column named “fraction deuterated”. Suggested fix: compute frac_deut only when percent = FALSE, or divide by 100 * nb_prot in the percent branch — or simply stop() for percent = TRUE.

[R/output_prep.R:78] FD2 writes 100 into the standard-deviation column, and 100 as an uptake in Daltons

Bug: the diff changed three rep(0, ...) to rep(100, ...). Only one of those three columns survives into the output as a mean; another survives as a standard deviation. The FD rows now report st.dev_Deut_Uptake = 100. In addition, in the default percent = FALSE branch the mean column is an uptake in Daltons, so 100 is not “100 %” — it is 100 Da. Evidence:

FD2<-data.frame(FD[,c(1,2,4:6,8,7,9)], rep(100,times=dim(FD)[1]),
                rep(100,times=dim(FD)[1]), rep(100,times=dim(FD)[1]))   # line 78
...
colnames(FD2)<-nm_final   # cols 9,10,11 -> st.dev_Peptide_Mass, Mean.Deut.Uptake, st.dev_Deut_Uptake
out<-out[,c(1:8,10:11)]   # line 123 drops col 9, KEEPS 10 (mean) and 11 (sd)

[reproduced] FD rows in the written csv:

Protein.State Deut.Time ... Mean.Deut.Uptake_.Da. st.dev_Deut_Uptake
      Unbound        FD ...                   100                100

and in percent = TRUE mode: Mean.Percent_Deut_.Da. = 100, st.dev_Percent_Deut = 100. Impact: output_prep() is explicitly “output ready for publication” (Masson et al. 2019 format). Every FD row now ships a bogus SD of 100, and in uptake mode a bogus mean of 100 Da. This is a regression introduced by the uncommitted diff — before it the values were 0, which was wrong for percent mode but at least not a fake SD. Suggested fix: make the three constants branch-aware. Something like: SD column always 0; mean column 100 when percent = TRUE and FD[,10] (the real FD X..Deut) when percent = FALSE. i.e. move the FD2/undeut2 construction inside the if (percent==FALSE) ... else ... block where nm_final is already branch-specific.

[R/sd_ci_timepoint.R:24-26] CI→SD conversion is ~2.5× too large (missing factor of 2, wrong t quantile)

Bug: the cited source (Cochrane 7.7.3.2, in the roxygen block) gives SE = (UL - LL) / (2 * t_{1-alpha/2, df}) and SD = SE * sqrt(N). The code omits the factor of 2 and uses qt(alpha, ...) (a one-tailed quantile) where the two-sided t.test(conf.level = 1-alpha) interval requires qt(alpha/2, ...). Evidence:

tvalue=abs(qt(alpha, replicates*2-2))                     # line 24: should be alpha/2
tt<-t.test(x1, x2, conf.level = c(1-alpha))               # two-sided interval
sd.ci<-(tt$conf.int[2]-tt$conf.int[1])/tvalue*sqrt(replicates)   # line 26: missing /2

For alpha = 0.01, replicates = 3: code uses t = |qt(0.01,4)| = 3.747, correct is 2 * |qt(0.005,4)| = 2 * 4.604 = 9.21. Ratio = 2.46× overestimate. Impact: sd_ci_timepoint() is the default SD source for plot_fissure_vent() (sd_source = "CI"). Every uncertainty ellipse is ~2.5× too big and the global CI band derived from those SDs (CI_2pts) is ~2.5× too wide, so significant peptides are under-called. This is a statistical-correctness bug, not cosmetic. Suggested fix:

tvalue <- abs(qt(alpha/2, replicates*2-2))
sd.ci  <- (tt$conf.int[2]-tt$conf.int[1]) / (2*tvalue) * sqrt(replicates)

(Also consider using tt$parameter, the Welch df, rather than replicates*2-2.) Update the formula in the roxygen block and in plot_fissure_vent.R’s @details, which repeat the same wrong formula.

[R/plot_fissure_vent.R:123] The plot’s y axis is built from state1, not state2

Bug: both arguments to plot() are av_state1. The y-axis range is therefore derived from state1’s data, not state2’s. Evidence:

plot(av1[, av_state1], av1[, av_state1], type = "n", xlab = "", ylab = "",
     xlim = xlim, ylim = ylim, ...)                       # line 123

Impact: whenever the two states have different value ranges (which is the entire point of the plot) ellipses for state2 are drawn partly or wholly off-canvas, with no warning. Inherited verbatim from plot_cor_pts_elps (R/correlation_functions_2states.R:24 has the identical plot(av1[,7], av1[,7], ...)), so it was not fixed by 868a44f. Suggested fix: plot(av1[, av_state1], av1[, av_state2], ...).

[R/residue_deconvolution.R:76-82] peptide_exch_residues() includes one residue too many — contradicts nb_exch_deut()

Bug: the roxygen says the helper matches nb_exch_deut()’s convention (“the first residue of each peptide and all Prolines are excluded”). nb_exch_deut() actually excludes the first two residues: (End-Start) - nP + firstP - 1 = L - 2 - nP_after_first. The helper starts at local index 2, giving L - 1 - nP_after_first — one extra residue per peptide. Evidence:

peptide_exch_residues <- function(start, seq_string) {
  chars <- strsplit(seq_string, "")[[1]]
  if (length(chars) < 2) return(integer(0))
  local_idx <- 2:length(chars)                 # <- line 79, should be 3:length(chars)
  resid_idx <- start + local_idx - 1
  resid_idx[chars[local_idx] != "P"]
}

vs R/nb_exchangeable_protons.R:15-16:

nb_exch_deut<-c(c(df$End-df$Start)-str_count(df$Sequence,'P') ) +
  as.numeric(substr(df$Sequence, 1, 1)=="P")-1

[reproduced] for all 128 peptides in the shipped example, length(peptide_exch_residues(...)) - nb_exch_deut(...) == 1 (every single row). Impact: the design matrix A spreads each peptide’s observed uptake over one extra residue, so every per-residue estimate is systematically diluted at the peptide’s N-terminal shoulder, and residue Start+1 (which the rest of the package treats as non-exchangeable) is assigned a spurious value. Also breaks the vignette’s cross-validation section, which copy-pastes the same helper (vignettes/HDXBoxeR.Rmd, “Choosing lambda_smooth”) — so the CV is fit and scored with the same off-by-one and cannot detect it. Suggested fix:

if (length(chars) < 3) return(integer(0))
local_idx <- 3:length(chars)

and mirror the change in the vignette chunk. Better: factor the helper out as a real (possibly non-exported) function so nb_exch_deut(), the deconvolution, and the vignette all share one definition — length(peptide_exch_residues(...)) == nb_exch_deut(...) would then be a natural unit test.

Severity 2 — inconsistent / misleading results, R CMD check breakage

[R/residue_level_average.R:58] Coverage window is off by one and ignores Prolines

Bug: the comment claims the window matches “the exchangeable-residue convention used elsewhere in this package”, but it uses Start+1 .. End (excludes only residue 1) and does no Proline exclusion at all. nb_exch_deut() excludes the first two residues and all non-first Prolines; residue_deconvolution() (after fixing the bug above) excludes first-two + Prolines. Evidence:

## a residue is covered if it falls within (Start+1)..End, matching
## the exchangeable-residue convention used elsewhere in this package
covering <- (sub$Start + 1) <= r & sub$End >= r        # line 58

[reproduced] with the example data, residue 41 (a Proline — first peptide is GPLGSK... at Start 40) is reported as covered by residue_level_average() but is NA in residue_deconvolution(). Impact: the two functions are documented as directly comparable baselines, but they disagree about which residues even exist. Prolines get fabricated uptake values in the averaged output. Suggested fix: use the same shared peptide_exch_residues() helper as residue_deconvolution() to decide coverage, rather than an inline range test.

[R/boxer_input_to_long.R:20,22] gather() and str_split_fixed() are used but not imported

Bug: neither tidyr::gather nor stringr::str_split_fixed appears in NAMESPACE. NAMESPACE only has importFrom(tidyr, separate) and importFrom(stringr, str_count) / importFrom(stringr, str_sub). Evidence: grep '^import' NAMESPACE → no gather, no str_split_fixed. Impact: R CMD check NOTE “no visible global function definition for ‘gather’ / ‘str_split_fixed’”; at runtime the function errors in an installed package unless the user happens to have tidyr/stringr attached. It only worked in my test because I library()d them manually. Suggested fix: add @importFrom tidyr gather and @importFrom stringr str_split_fixed (and re-roxygenize). Note tidyr::gather() is retired-superseded; tidyr::pivot_longer() would be the forward-looking choice.

[NAMESPACE] boxer_input_to_long and all_data_long_input have man pages but are not exported

Bug: the NAMESPACE diff adds only plot_fissure_vent, residue_deconvolution, residue_level_average. Neither function in boxer_input_to_long.R carries an @export tag, yet man/boxer_input_to_long.Rd and man/all_data_long_input.Rd were generated. Evidence: grep boxer_input_to_long NAMESPACE → no match; man/boxer_input_to_long.Rd exists with a full \usage{} block. Impact: users cannot call HDXBoxeR::boxer_input_to_long(). R CMD check also emits “Rd sections for objects not exported”. (Four pre-existing Rd files have the same problem: deuteration_woods_timecourse_frac, is.nan.data.frame, plot_cor_pts_elps, sd_ci_timepoint — worth cleaning up in the same pass.) Suggested fix: add @export to both roxygen blocks (they clearly document user-facing arguments), or add @keywords internal / @noRd if they are meant to be internal.

[tests/ — missing tests/testthat.R] the test suite never runs

Bug: tests/testthat/test-residue_deconvolution.R exists but there is no tests/testthat.R driver file. DESCRIPTION correctly has testthat (>= 3.0.0) in Suggests and Config/testthat/edition: 3, but without the driver R CMD check finds no runnable test file in tests/. Evidence: ls tests tests/testthat → tests/ contains only the testthat/ directory. Impact: all four tests are dead weight — R CMD check reports 0 tests run, and CI would pass on a completely broken residue_deconvolution(). Suggested fix: create tests/testthat.R containing:

library(testthat)
library(HDXBoxeR)

test_check("HDXBoxeR")

(usethis::use_testthat(3) does this.)

Separately, on the tests themselves: they run and pass conceptually (I checked the assertions against real output: nrow == 225*4 == 900 ✓; the two expect_error cases both really do hit the stop() because the two column-name regexes are mutually exclusive — _X\.\.Deut_[0-9]+$ vs _Deut\.\._[0-9]+$ ✓; deconvolution values fall in [0,1] ✓; averaged values fall in [10.8, 102.8] ✓). But every assertion is a shape/bounds check. Nothing tests numerical correctness, which is why the off-by-one in peptide_exch_residues() (bug above) sails straight through. Worth adding: - a synthetic-data round trip: build peptides with known per-residue uptake, check A %*% x_hat ≈ b; - length(peptide_exch_residues(Start, Sequence)) == nb_exch_deut(row) for every row; - lambda_smooth = 0 vs > 0 actually changes the result (currently untested); - an NA residue for a region with no peptide coverage.

[man/plot_fissure_vent.Rd] Rd file is stale relative to the R source — R CMD check WARNING

Bug: the .Rd was generated from an older version of the roxygen block. It documents an argument sd that does not exist, and omits four that do. Evidence: \usage{} lists position_col, deut, length1, xlim; \arguments{} has no \item for any of them, but does have \item{sd}{flag. CI (default) ...} — the argument is actually named sd_source. The \examples{} block calls woods_CI_plot_frac() and output_tc(), i.e. it never calls plot_fissure_vent() at all. Impact: R CMD check → WARNING “Undocumented arguments in documentation object ‘plot_fissure_vent’: ‘position_col’ ‘deut’ ‘length1’ ‘xlim’” and “Documented arguments not in … : ‘sd’”. The R source is fine (it has @param sd_source, @param xlim); only the Rd is stale. But position_col, deut and length1 are undocumented in the source too. Suggested fix: re-run roxygen2::roxygenise(), and add @param position_col, @param length1 to R/plot_fissure_vent.R. deut (line 55) is accepted but never referenced anywhere in the body — delete it.

[R/plot_fissure_vent.R:60] Default state1/state2 are truncated by an off-by-one str_sub()

Bug: end = -10 strips 9 trailing characters, but the suffix on an averaged column (av_Unbound_X..Deut) is _X..Deut, 8 characters. Evidence:

nm1 <- str_sub(colnames(av1)[7:ncol(av1)], start = 4, end = -10)   # line 60
if (missing(state1)) state1 <- nm1[1]

[reproduced] uptake input → nm1 = c("Unboun", "boun"); percent input (suffix _Deut.., 7 chars) → nm1 = c("Unbou", "bou"). Impact: currently masked, because resolve_col()/resolve_raw_cols() use startsWith() and a truncated prefix still matches. It stops being masked as soon as two states share a prefix that only differs in the last character(s) — e.g. "State1" / "State2" truncate to "State" / "Stat", and resolve_col() then throws “State ‘State’ matches multiple columns”. Also the truncated string is what appears in any user-facing error message. Suggested fix: don’t count characters. Derive the root by stripping the known suffix: sub("^av_", "", sub("_(X\\.\\.Deut|Deut\\.\\.)$", "", colnames(av1)[7:ncol(av1)])).

[R/plot_fissure_vent.R:49] The @examples block passes a numeric times and silently produces an empty plot

Bug: Deut.Time values are character ("3.00s", "60.00s", …). The example passes times = 3.00. select_indices() compares df$Deut.Time == 3.00, which is FALSE everywhere. Evidence:

#' plot_fissure_vent(df = a, replicates = 3, times = 3.00, alpha = 0.01,
#'                    pvalue = 0.01, state1 = "Unbound", state2 = "bound")   # line 49-50

[reproduced] times = 3.00 → ind1 empty → CI_2pts() on a zero-length vector → message: "time 3: CI = NaN", plot drawn with zero peptides, no error or warning. times = "3.00s" → "time 3.00s: CI = 1.607" and peptides drawn. Impact: the documented example produces a blank plot. More importantly the function gives no feedback for an unmatched times value, so a user typo yields a silently empty figure. Suggested fix: change the example to times = "3.00s", and add a guard in the loop: if (length(ind1) == 0) { warning(sprintf("no peptides match times = '%s'", times[i])); next }.

[R/robot_indexes_df.R:43-44] replicates argument is ignored when computing the CI

Bug: replicates = 3 is hardcoded in the prep_timecourse_plot_sd() call, while the sibling function robot_indexes() (line 99-100 of the same file) correctly passes replicates = replicates. Evidence:

# robot_indexes_df, line 43:
CI_all<-prep_timecourse_plot_sd(control_df_up, variant_df_up, replicates=3, alpha=alpha)
# robot_indexes, line 99:
CI_all<-prep_timecourse_plot_sd(control_df_up, variant_df_up, replicates=replicates, alpha)

Impact: for any dataset with ≠3 replicates, robot_indexes_df() computes the CI threshold with the wrong t-value and wrong pooled-SD normalization, so it returns the wrong significant-peptide set — while pv_timecourse() and prep_timecourse_plot_ave() in the same function use the correct replicates. Silent. Suggested fix: replicates = replicates.

[R/robot_indexes_df.R:26-56 and :82-109] Multi-state loop discards all but the last state

Bug: peptide_all <- c() is re-initialized inside the for (state in ...) loop, and sig_pep is built after the loop. With more than 2 protein states, the significant peptides found for every state except the last are thrown away. Evidence:

for ( state in states[2:length(states)]) {
    ...
    peptide_all<-c()                                   # line 46: reset each iteration
    for (i in 7:dim(sh_avc)[2]) { peptide_all<-c(peptide_all, which(...)) }
    peptide_all<-sort(unique(peptide_all))
  }                                                    # line 52: loop ends
  sig_pep<-data.frame(1:length(peptide_all), sh_avc[peptide_all,c(1:3,5)])   # line 54

Identical structure in robot_indexes() (lines 82-109). Impact: the docs say “As default all states are chosen”, but the returned peptide set reflects only states[1] vs states[length(states)]. Also note sh_avc used on line 54 is the last iteration’s version — consistent by accident, not by design. Suggested fix: move peptide_all <- c() above the for (state ...) loop and drop the mid-loop reset (or accumulate into a list keyed by state and return that).

[R/correlation_functions_2states.R:38-39] The ellipse bug fixed in plot_fissure_vent still exists here

Bug: plot_cor_pts_elps() is the function plot_fissure_vent() was derived from. Its first branch divides the ellipse y-centre by 2 and applies /2 to only one of the two radii — exactly the bug commit 868a44f fixed in plot_fissure_vent.R. The second branch (line 51) has it right. Evidence:

# line 38-39, is.na(position_col) branch  -- WRONG
DrawEllipse(av1[i,state1], av1[i,state2]/2, sd1[i,state1]/2,
            sd1[i,state2], ...)
# line 51-52, else branch                 -- CORRECT
DrawEllipse(av1[i,state1], av1[i,state2], sd1[i,state1]/2, sd1[i,state2]/2,
            col = position_col[i], border= position_col[i], ...)

Impact: the default call path of plot_cor_pts_elps() (no position_col supplied) draws every ellipse at half its correct y position with a y-radius 2× too large. plot_cor_pts_elps is used by the exported plot_correlation_functions family. Suggested fix: make line 38 match line 51: DrawEllipse(av1[i,state1], av1[i,state2], sd1[i,state1]/2, sd1[i,state2]/2, ...). Same file line 24 also has the plot(av1[,7], av1[,7], ...) duplicated-axis bug.

Severity 3 — edge cases, robustness

[R/plot_fissure_vent.R:140,155-156] Significance threshold is CI/2, but the rest of the package uses CI

Bug: the roxygen block claims the peptide outline uses “the same two-part standard as the rest of this package (CI_2pts + a p-value cutoff)”. It doesn’t — it halves the CI. Evidence:

is_sig <- (delta > ci / 2) && !is.na(pv_state1v2[pep]) && (pv_state1v2[pep] < pvalue)  # line 140
points(c(-10, 110), c(-10, 110) + ci / 2, type = "l", col = "grey")                    # line 155

vs everywhere else in the package:

R/inside_functions_plot.R:45   abs1 <- abs(df_av[,i]) > CI[i-7]
R/list_significantly_different_peptides.R:33  abs.a <- abs(df1[...,i]) > CI
R/robot_indexes_df.R:49        abs(sh_avc_up[,i]-sh_avv_up[,i]) > CI_all[i-6]

Impact: twice as many peptides are flagged significant here as by list_significantly_different_peptides() / the robot plots on the same data. The /2 was inherited from plot_cor_pts_elps (where it was only a drawing convention with no significance call attached); plot_fissure_vent promoted it to a statistical decision. Note the ~2.5× SD inflation in sd_ci_timepoint (Severity 1) partly cancels this, which is why it doesn’t look obviously wrong on the example data. Suggested fix: decide which convention is intended and make band + test agree — either draw at ±ci and test delta > ci, or keep the visual ±ci/2 band but document clearly that it is a half-band and test against ci.

[R/residue_level_average.R:51] 1 / nb_exch_deut() can be Inf or negative

Bug: no guard on the weight denominator. nb_exch_deut() returns L - 2 - nP_after_first, which is 0 for a 2-residue peptide (or e.g. PGP-heavy short peptides) and can go negative for a short Proline-rich peptide. Evidence:

w <- 1 / nb_exch_deut(sub)     # line 51
...
res_mat[r, ] <- colSums(vals * wi * ok, na.rm = TRUE) / colSums(wi * ok, na.rm = TRUE)

Impact: a zero → Inf weight makes the whole residue Inf/Inf = NaN; a negative weight silently produces a weighted mean outside the data range. Not triggered by the shipped example (range(nb_exch_deut(a)) == c(5, 19)), so it will show up only on a user’s dataset with short peptides — the worst kind of latent bug. Suggested fix: drop rows with nb_exch_deut(sub) <= 0 before weighting, and warn.

[R/residue_level_average.R:63] Uncovered/all-NA columns yield NaN, not NA

Bug: if every covering peptide has NA in a given column, the denominator colSums(wi * ok, na.rm = TRUE) is 0 and the result is NaN rather than the documented NA. Evidence:

res_mat[r, ] <- colSums(vals * wi * ok, na.rm = TRUE) / colSums(wi * ok, na.rm = TRUE)  # line 63

Doc says: “NA where no peptide covers a residue.” Impact: is.na() catches NaN so most downstream code is fine, but plotting and identical()/comparison code that distinguishes them will not be. Minor. Suggested fix: den <- colSums(wi*ok, na.rm=TRUE); res_mat[r, ] <- ifelse(den > 0, num/den, NA_real_).

[R/sd_ave_diff_pv_tp.R:17,47,82 and R/sd_ci_timepoint.R:17] str_sub(nm_root, end = -3) breaks with ≥10 replicates

Bug: the root name is derived by chopping a fixed 2 characters, assuming the replicate suffix is always _1.._9. Evidence: (identical line in all four functions)

nm_root<-colnames(df[,c(6+((1:nb_sets)-1)*replicates+1)])
nm_root<-str_sub(nm_root, end = -3)      # "Unbound_X..Deut_1" -> "Unbound_X..Deut"

Impact: with replicates >= 10 the first column of a set is still _1, so this happens to survive — but any code path that reaches _10 gets "Unbound_X..Deut_". Combined with the end = -10 truncation in plot_fissure_vent.R:60, column-name parsing in this package is character-count based throughout and will misbehave on unusual state names. Low priority but worth a systematic fix. Suggested fix: sub("_[0-9]+$", "", nm_root).

[R/plot_fissure_vent.R:56,123,145] ... is forwarded to both plot() and DrawEllipse()

Bug: @param ... is documented as “other plotting parameters, passed to DrawEllipse”, but the same ... also goes to plot(). Evidence:

plot(av1[, av_state1], av1[, av_state1], type = "n", ..., ...)   # line 123
DrawEllipse(..., col = fill_col, border = border_col, ...)       # line 145

Impact: any DrawEllipse-specific argument (nv, plot, angle) reaches plot.default() → par() and produces “… is not a graphical parameter” warnings on every call; conversely plot-only arguments reach DrawEllipse. Also col/border are set explicitly on line 145, so a user passing col = gets “formal argument matched by multiple actual arguments”. Suggested fix: either restrict ... to DrawEllipse (and give plot() its own explicit args) or add a separate ellipse_args = list() parameter.

[vignettes/HDXBoxeR.Rmd, “Choosing lambda_smooth”] The CV chunk is eval’d and re-fits the deconvolution 12 times

Bug: the cross-validation chunk has no eval=FALSE / cache=TRUE, and runs residue_deconvolution() for 4 λ values × 3 folds. Evidence: for (lam in lambda_grid) { for (f in 1:k) { fit <- residue_deconvolution(train_df, protein_length = 225, lambda_smooth = lam) ... } } Impact: adds ~12× a single fit (≈0.6 s each on the shipped 128-peptide example, so tolerable here) to every R CMD check / vignette build, and scales badly for anyone who adapts it. It also silently re-defines peptide_exch_residues() with the same off-by-one as the package internal, so the CV cannot detect that bug. Suggested fix: eval = FALSE on the chunk (it’s illustrative), and call the shared package helper instead of re-defining it.
